sources: THURSDAY Oct 29 2026 RUN, pre-US-open (before 13:30 UTC), DAY AFTER THE FOMC. This run has WEDNESDAY'S FULL US CLOSES plus FRED prints through Oct 27-28 and the new Oct 23 NFCI, so only MOVE and the two plumbing tiles are carries. HEADLINE: THE FED HELD IN A SPLIT HAWKISH VOTE, THE LONG END SOLD OFF AND THE CURVE STEEPENED HARD OFF ITS OCTOBER LOW. FOMC - HOLD AT 3.75-4.00 PCT, TWO HAWKISH DISSENTS. The Committee kept the target range at 3-3/4 to 4 pct on a 10-2 vote; COOK AND HAMMACK BOTH DISSENTED IN FAVOUR OF A 25BP HIKE. The statement calls activity 'growing briskly' with strong productivity and robust capital investment, says hiring has roughly matched workforce growth with the unemployment rate barely moved, and describes inflation as STILL HIGH, adding that the Committee 'will deliver price stability'. No change to QT; the ample-reserves policy is reaffirmed. Chair Warsh signalled no rush and said politics played no role ahead of the midterms; officials pointed to December data. So the hawkish tail, not the dovish one, is what got repriced. CURVE - THE BIGGEST SINGLE-DAY STEEPENING OF THE MONTH. FRED T10Y2Y Oct 28 at 0.38, up 9bp from Oct 27's 0.29 and a FULL REVERSAL of the new October low set the day before (0.32 Oct 26, 0.31 Oct 23, 0.31 Oct 22, 0.32 Oct 21). Versus 0.32 a week ago the tile flips from DOWN to UP. The mechanism is clean and all in the long end: the 2Y barely moved at 4.731 pct (minus under 1bp) because Warsh promised nothing, while the 10Y rose 5.2bp to 5.044 pct, its biggest gain since Sep 28, and the 30Y rose 5.6bp to 5.360 pct. NOTE A REAL SOURCE DISPERSION HERE: the cash tape implies a 2s10s of about 31bp while FRED's constant-maturity H.15 series prints 0.38; the tile follows FRED for continuity with every prior run, but treat the LEVEL as 0.31-0.38 and the DIRECTION (sharply steeper) as the reliable signal. BREAKEVEN - THE FIVE-SESSION BREAK IS OVER. FRED T5YIFR Oct 27 at 2.25 pct, up 4bp on the day from 2.21 (2.20 Oct 23, 2.19 Oct 22, 2.34 Oct 21). Still 9bp BELOW the 2.34 of a week ago so the tile stays DOWN, but the floor is in and the direction has turned up for the first time since the oil spike began. Combined with the long-end selloff this is the market starting - tentatively - to price the oil premium and a hawkish Fed into the inflation path, which is exactly what the last four runs flagged as the missing piece. CREDIT - THE MONTH WIDE IS FULLY REPAIRED AND THEN SOME. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 Oct 27 at 3.18 pct, 12bp TIGHTER on the day from 3.30 and 22bp inside the Oct 22 month wide of 3.40 (3.38 Oct 23, 3.27 Oct 21). Tile 330 to 318bp. Versus 327bp a week ago that is minus 9bp, so the trend flips to DOWN and HY is now at its TIGHTEST of October. Wednesday's cash commentary had HY tightening a further 8bp with investment grade steady near 90bp. The Oct 22-23 credit scare is not just unwound, it has overshot. VOL - EQUITY VOL AT A NEW MONTH LOW, THIRD GREEN SESSION. VIX 16.91 for the Oct 28 close, minus 3.48 pct from 17.52, confirmed by two independent sources; FRED VIXCLS has posted Oct 27 at 17.52 and now shows the Oct 21-23 sequence revised to 16.68, 19.03 and 19.45. That is the LOWEST VIX of October. Against 16.68 on Oct 21 it is plus 1.4 pct, so the tile stays FLAT while the level sits at the bottom of the range. Equities closed green for a third straight session: S&P 500 7,743.98 plus 0.28 pct, Nasdaq Composite 26,549.85 plus 0.27 pct, Dow 52,475.10 plus 0.19 pct, energy leading and real estate and utilities lagging. MOVE is CARRIED at 103.31 for Oct 23 for a FOURTEENTH consecutive blind run - Investing.com still stops at Oct 23 (106.84 Oct 22, 95.94 Oct 21, 101.70 Oct 20, 101.30 Oct 19, 101.10 Oct 16). Against Oct 20 (101.70) the carry would read plus 1.6 pct so the tile is held FLAT. This is now the single most stale input on the board and it is stale precisely when rate vol is the thing that moved: a 5.6bp jump in the 30Y on an FOMC day is exactly what MOVE exists to measure. TREAT THE MOVE TILE AS BLIND, NOT AS CALM. OIL - THE PREMIUM FINALLY FADES ON IRAN DIPLOMACY. Brent 114.10 USD minus 1.06 pct (TradingEconomics stats 114.06 minus 1.10 pct; HDFC 114.2 minus 1 pct), WTI 101.43 minus 1.32 pct, after a STRONG Wednesday that closed Brent 115.32 plus 1.26 pct and WTI 102.78 plus 2.88 pct. The fade is diplomatic, not physical: US VP Vance is reported to have written to Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei seeking to revive peace talks, Qatari mediators have put a draft war-ending proposal to Tehran (an Iranian official called it not a formal offer), and Iran's foreign minister said Wednesday that Tehran is still giving diplomacy a chance. ON THE SUPPLY SIDE THE RISK IS STILL LIVE AND STILL UNCONFIRMED: the Houthi claim on the 550,000 b/d Saudi refinery remains unconfirmed by Riyadh for an ELEVENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN, and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired at the eastern region early Thursday. So interceptions keep being confirmed and damage never is. Versus 111.20 a week ago Brent is plus 2.6 pct, trend still UP. INVENTORIES SURPRISED TIGHT: US crude stocks FELL 1.9 million barrels in the week ended Oct 23 against an expected plus 15,000, while gasoline ROSE 3.9 million against an expected 900,000 draw - a crude draw with a gasoline build, i.e. weak implied demand behind a tight crude number. METALS - COPPER-GOLD HOLDS A NEW HIGH. Gold 4,027.59 USD/t.oz minus 0.99 pct this morning after 4,051.60 December futures minus 0.53 pct Wednesday and an earlier 4,034.98 print; copper 6.60 to 6.6150 USD/Lbs, minus 0.47 to 0.65 pct. Copper-gold 6.61/4027.59*1000 = 1.641, tile 1.64, unchanged from last run and up from 1.57 a week ago. Trend UP, fourth consecutive run of improvement, still the cleanest pro-growth signal on the board. DOLLAR - THE FLIP TO UP DOES NOT HOLD. DXY 102.14 (TradingEconomics 102.138 minus 0.18 pct, text summary 102.104 minus 0.21 pct) after a 102.16 minus 0.16 pct Wednesday close. Versus 101.79 on Oct 21 that is plus 0.34 pct, HALF last run's week-on-week move and inside noise, so the tile goes BACK TO FLAT after one run at up. A hawkish split vote did not buy the dollar, which is worth noting. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - NEW PRINT, NO CHANGE. The NFCI for the week ending OCT 23 HAS POSTED at minus 0.49, the first read containing both the Oct 22 and Oct 23 risk-off sessions, and it shows essentially NOTHING: minus 0.49 against minus 0.496 the week before is within rounding. CAVEAT ON PRECISION: the only source serving the Oct 23 value this morning quotes TWO DECIMALS (usmacro.com, updated Oct 28, next update Nov 4); FRED's series page was still serving Oct 16 at minus 0.496 when read. So the tile is minus 0.49 at two-decimal precision, trend FLAT, and the third decimal should be re-read next run. The read-through matters: the two-day credit and vol scare never reached broad financial conditions at all. MACRO TILES - ALL CARRIED, TWO RELEASES DUE TODAY AFTER THIS RUN. Jobless claims 194k week ending Oct 17 (three-month low) versus 199k a week ago, trend down; continuing claims about 1.73 million, a six-week high - little firing, visibly less hiring; THE NEXT PRINT IS TODAY Oct 29 at 8:30 ET / 12:30 UTC, AFTER this run. The Fed H.4.1 is ALSO TODAY, after this run, so global liquidity stays at 1 (stable) on the Oct 21 sheet: total assets 6,753,604 million USD, minus 2,035 million on the week, plus 2.5 pct on the year, no regime change at the ECB, PBOC or BOJ. LEI y/y plus 1.2 pct September (index 99.6) versus minus 0.7 pct a week ago, trend up, still the biggest week-on-week improvement on the board. Consumer sentiment 48.0 UMich October final versus 46.3, trend up, though 48.0 is still a five-month low in level. ISM Manufacturing 54.5 September, next Nov 2. Sahm Rule 0.00 September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50. Building permits 1,400k SAAR September, next mid-November. MONETARY PLUMBING - BLIND, FOURTEENTH RUN. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION at 0bp, NOT a measurement; every free source serves a SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is likewise a STANDING ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp. Two assumed tiles plus one judgement tile (global liquidity) plus one stale tile (MOVE) out of eighteen - unchanged for a fourteenth run. CALENDAR: jobless claims TODAY 8:30 ET. September PCE TODAY. H.4.1 TODAY. OPEC+ Sunday Nov 1 (expected to hold December targets). ISM Nov 2. US midterms Nov 3. Sahm Nov 6. NFCI Nov 4. Next FOMC December. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD 35c8b7d, Oct 28 commit), this scheduled session remains the SOLE writer of data.json, the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17, BDTI stays removed since Oct 17. The .git lock-file pile keeps growing (HEAD.lock, HEAD.lock.*.bak, index.lock.* and similar, roughly 170 now) because this session cannot delete files in the folder; still harmless but it WILL eventually break a git operation and clearing it needs delete permission on the Dashboard Macro folder. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, FOURTEENTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in PLAIN TEXT in .git/config; it is fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Untracked junk still in the repo root: _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: the board has turned over. For four runs the story was GROWTH-OK, INFLATION-FADING, CURVE-FLATTENING with a live dovish tail. The hold-with-two-hike-dissents killed that tail, and the response was textbook: the 2Y did not move, the long end sold off, the curve steepened 9bp off its October low, and the breakeven stopped falling. Simultaneously the risk tiles are the best of the month - VIX at a month low, HY at a month tight, three green equity sessions, copper-gold at a new high, LEI positive, claims at a three-month low - and the oil premium is fading on Iran diplomacy rather than on confirmed barrels. That combination, cheap risk plus a steepening curve plus a Fed that says inflation is still high, is NOT the recession setup the flattening was hinting at; it is a reflation-and-term-premium setup. The two things that would break it are both knowable soon: a confirmed hit on Saudi crude infrastructure, and today's PCE. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: September PCE today, the first inflation print the market must reconcile with 'inflation is still high' and two hike dissents; today's jobless claims after three weeks of improving level and deteriorating continuing claims; whether T10Y2Y holds above 0.35 or the steepening was a one-day FOMC artifact; whether T5YIFR keeps climbing from 2.25 now that the long end has repriced; whether Riyadh ever confirms damage at the refinery, and whether the Iran talks become a formal offer; OPEC+ Sunday; getting a live MOVE print, which is now the board's worst blind spot; rotating the embedded PAT; clearing the .git lock files.
